questions.question: What did the Preacher test by pursuing pleasure, building, and wealth?
options: Whether it brought lasting meaning, but found it all vanity
Whether hard work could earn him favor with God
Whether wealth could secure his good name for all generations
Whether a king was permitted to enjoy such pleasures
questions.answer: Whether it brought lasting meaning, but found it all vanity

questions.question: What troubled the Preacher about his labor?
options: Other greedy men were always stealing away the profit of his hard work
He must leave it to one who comes after him, who may be a fool
God himself had wholly forbidden him to enjoy any of its good fruit
It had earned him no real wealth and no lasting reputation at all
questions.answer: He must leave it to one who comes after him, who may be a fool

questions.question: The Preacher concludes there is nothing better than to eat, drink, and find enjoyment in toil, which is from the hand of God.
I made great works; I built houses and planted _____ for myself.
Then I considered all that my hands had done, and behold, all was vanity and a striving after _____.
